candidates.source_name: Athanasius of Alexandria / Epistulae ad Serapionem 1.30
candidates.source_attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Epistulae ad Serapionem de Spiritu Sancto (Letters to Serapion on the Holy Spirit, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).
candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria Epistulae ad Serapionem 1.30 (c. 350 AD)

'But he, being full of the Holy Ghost, looked up stedfastly into heaven, and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God' — Athanasius marks Stephanos plērēs Pneumatos Hagiou (Stephen full of the Holy Spirit) eiden doxan theou kai Iēsoun (saw glory-of-God and Jesus) as the TRINITARIAN-EYE-WITNESS martyrdom-scene: Stephen, IN-the-Spirit, sees the Father-glory + the Son-at-the-right-hand. All three divine Persons are simultaneously-participated-in the witness. The 'standing' (hestōta) — distinct from the usual seated-at-right-hand — is the rare-Acts iconography of Christ-rising-to-receive-the-martyr.
